head_commit.message:
replay: historical pages show historical state

Four findings from the second audit, all confirmed in the code first.

The account editor on a replayed page was filled from today's chain, so the
values you edit — and the scenarios generated from them — described today
rather than the slot on screen. It now describes the accounts the replay
actually started from. On the audit's own Orca case the fee payer reads
15,793,378,961, the replay's pre-state, where it used to read today's
15,788,933,176.

The account-changes stream carries bytes and owner but no balance, so an
account rebuilt from it took today's lamports while the certificate called
it Recorded. It now prefers the balance in the transaction's own record,
which is exact at the slot that record describes, and when it cannot, the
account is reported as drifted rather than vouched for.

A date lookup returned whatever its sixth estimate reached, landing 102
seconds from the time asked for. It now keeps the closest block, walks
until it is within two seconds, and refuses rather than guess if nothing is
within a minute. Impossible dates are rejected instead of rolling forward,
so February 30 is an error, not March 2.

replay_at_slot never applied the 30-day window guard the other replay
routes enforce.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01WkmgCy2pK7G3U3xXoYQjSJ

head_commit.message:
server: a link a crowd is following stays cached

Answers were evicted and expired by when they were computed, so the one
transaction everyone is opening could be dropped to make room for answers
nobody asked for again. Reading an answer now refreshes it: eviction falls
on the cold entries instead. The world at a past slot does not change, so
serving an older answer stays correct.
